name: GPU via WebGL unmasked renderer
plain: Reads the graphics card and driver name through WebGL.
meaning: Exposes GPU model and driver (ANGLE (NVIDIA, GeForce RTX 4070 ...)). Identifies the device tier and OS. Safari reports a generic Apple GPU; Brave and Firefox spoof or trim it.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

safari.note: Generic Apple GPU string since Safari 15

limits.headline: Can see your graphics card and driver name through WebGL
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page draws 3D graphics or tests for it
can: See your GPU make and model, like an NVIDIA GeForce
See your driver and graphics layer
Guess your device tier and OS
Tune graphics settings to your GPU
cannot: See the exact GPU in Safari; it shows a generic Apple GPU
See the real name in Brave or Firefox when they hide it
See your files or screen contents
Work if graphics support is off
limits.differs: Safari shows a generic Apple GPU. Brave and Firefox hide or trim the name.

story.what_it_is: Reads the name of your graphics card and driver through the browser's 3D drawing tool.
story.for_you: You never see it. A game or video site reads your graphics chip name to pick settings, for example turning on high detail for a strong card. Safari shows a generic name to protect you.
story.for_makers: Graphics apps use the name to apply known fixes for specific chips and to choose a quality level. Fraud teams spot virtual machines by names like SwiftShader. Trackers use the exact name as a fingerprint piece.

use_cases.example: A browser game sees an RTX card and starts on ultra graphics, while a weak integrated chip gets low settings.
A cloud gaming site picks a different video decoder path for a known buggy graphics driver.
A bot defence service flags a visit that reports SwiftShader, which is how many headless servers draw graphics.
A support team reads the graphics name from a bug report to match a known driver bug.
An advertiser treats a high end graphics chip as a sign of a gaming PC and shows hardware ads.
A browser 3D design tool turns off heavy effects on integrated graphics.
A product team counts graphics chips to decide whether it can require newer features.

risks: Browsers like Safari and Brave hide or blur it

technical_bounds: No driver version precision on Safari
Extension can be disabled by browser policy

linkedin.how: WebGL renderer, vendor, extensions, 65+ parameters. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
